title: Safety and Red-Team Evaluations
summary: Measuring what a system should not do, and what it should not refuse. This lesson covers harmful-compliance and over-refusal metrics, honest jailbreak evaluation with attack budgets and good graders, prompt-injection evals for tool-using agents, the refusal trade-off, and how frontier labs use capability thresholds to decide when stronger safeguards are required.
objectives: After this lesson you can define harmful-compliance rate, over-refusal rate and attack success rate, and compute expected harm cost with base rates
Evaluate jailbreak robustness with an attack budget and correct an attack success rate for grader error
Design a prompt-injection eval for an agent that reports utility, utility under attack and targeted attack success
Choose a refusal threshold by weighing over-refusal against harmful compliance
Explain how frontier safety frameworks use capability evaluations, thresholds and elicitation
prerequisites: Prompt injection and attack success rate from [/learn/prompt-and-context/prompt-injection](/learn/prompt-and-context/prompt-injection), guardrail thresholds from [/learn/production-systems/guardrails](/learn/production-systems/guardrails), and judge calibration from [/learn/evaluation/eval-driven-development](/learn/evaluation/eval-driven-development).
